Source: https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/laravel.html

## Building on Laravel[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/laravel.html#building-on-laravel)

This page covers what a Laravel bake adds over the raw base and the practices that keep Laravel shapes sound. Start by picking your shape on [Pick a shape](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/shapes.html), then come back here for what the bake gives you and how to keep it healthy.

A Laravel loaf bakes from a fresh Laravel skeleton, not from the raw base: `sourdough new --laravel` starts from Composer's official installer and layers the stack on top, so the app inherits Laravel's upgrades to the skeleton.

### What a Laravel bake adds[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/laravel.html#what-a-laravel-bake-adds)

- `--laravel` bakes a Laravel + Blade app: a fresh Laravel skeleton from Composer, the laravel-blade overlay, the stack packages, Squire's laravel deploy files and the manifest.
- `--laravel --vue` bakes a Laravel + Blade + Vue islands app: the Laravel + Blade bake under a front-end layer (Vite with the Vue plugin, a `resources/js/app.js` registry that mounts a Vue 3 app on every `[data-vue-island]` element, and a Counter island live on the dashboard view).
- `--inertia` bakes a Laravel + Inertia/Vue app: the same Laravel skeleton, the laravel-inertia overlay (Inertia pages rendered by Vue and drawn by WayneUI: its app bar, sidebar, drawer, footer and components from `@waynestate/wayne-ui-css` and `@waynestate/wayne-ui-vue` 2.0.8, pinned exactly; no Tailwind; ESLint bans the old kit's `components/ui` imports; Ziggy routes; the stack packages; a `frontend` CI job that lints, type-checks and builds), Squire's laravel deploy files and the manifest.

All five permutations generate in 0.1; the raw ones (`--raw`, `--raw --vue`) start from the raw base instead of a Laravel skeleton.

### Build on the official installer[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/laravel.html#build-on-the-official-installer)

For Laravel paths, wrap the supported entry points instead of copying Laravel's skeleton by hand. `composer create-project laravel/laravel` picks the newest major, which is right. The installer also accepts a community starter kit published on Packagist:

```bash
laravel new my-app --using=vendor/kit
```

A kit declares its environment variables in `.env.example` and its setup steps in the `post-create-project-cmd` list of its `composer.json`. There is no plain Blade kit, so the `--laravel` (Blade) and Blade-plus-Vue-islands permutations are a bare Laravel install plus Sourdough's own layer, not a vendor kit.

### Local runtime: Sail or Docker[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/laravel.html#local-runtime-sail-or-docker)

The Laravel paths take a flag for the local runtime, and the two are mutually exclusive: together they are refused with `Choose one of --sail or --docker, not both.`

- `--sail` runs the app on Laravel Sail. The bake adds `laravel/sail` to require-dev, writes a `compose.yaml`, sets the database settings in `.env.example` and appends a "Run it locally with Sail" README section. The database is MySQL 8.4 LTS. Sail serves as its own `sail` user, so when the checkout is one that user cannot write (a Windows drive, or files a root container wrote), the compose file opens the app's files to it before Sail starts (`vendor/`, `node_modules/` and `.git` are left alone). Without that, every page was a 500 naming `tempnam()`. On a normal Linux or macOS checkout nothing changes.
- `--docker` writes the app's own Docker setup after the shape is baked: a two-target `Dockerfile` (dev and prod) whose base images are pinned by manifest-list digest, a `compose.yaml` with a MySQL 8.4 service (and a vite service for the Vue and Inertia shapes, which runs `npm install` on its first start and then `npm run dev` with `LARAVEL_SAIL=1` so `public/hot` says `http://localhost:5173`, an address your browser can load), a `.dockerignore`, the PHP ini files the image copies in, the `composer dev-up`, `dev-down` and `dev-shell` scripts, the database settings in `.env.example`, and a "Run it locally with Docker" README section. It works natively on Windows, macOS and Linux (no WSL2 needed) and is checked on amd64 and arm64.

Sail is Laravel's Docker development environment. On Windows it needs WSL2 and its `sail` script is shell, so it is an option where it fits, never the only Windows route; `--docker` is the route that works natively. See [Every developer, every operating system](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/every-os.html) for the full picture.

With `--docker`, the production build takes Playbook's credentials as a BuildKit secret, never a build arg:

```bash
docker build --target prod --secret id=composer_auth,src=auth.json -t myapp .
```

The `FROM` lines in the generated `Dockerfile` are the single place to swap in SQUIRE's Citadel-parity image when it exists.

### Sign-in stays SESAME[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/laravel.html#sign-in-stays-sesame)

Laravel's kits ship registration, password reset, email verification and two-factor login through Fortify. A WSU app signs in through SESAME, so turn off the features you do not use, and remove their routes from the front end too. In the Vue, React and Svelte kits a leftover reference to a disabled route breaks the build, because routes are generated at build time.

Warning

A live `/register` route in an app that is supposed to use central sign-in is a security hole and a support burden. The kits also set a login rate limit (5 a minute per email and IP in the docs' example), and the WorkOS variants would add a second hosted identity provider beside SESAME, so leave them out.

### Keep Boost current[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/laravel.html#keep-boost-current)

For the Inertia reference path, install Laravel Boost with `--dev`, and refresh its generated guideline and skill files with `boost:update`; the Boost docs suggest running it from Composer's `post-update-cmd`. Stale agent guidance teaches an agent last year's API. Boost runs on Laravel 10 to 13 with PHP 8.1 or higher. Its docs say the generated `.mcp.json`, guideline files (`CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `junie/`) and `boost.json` may go in `.gitignore`, because `boost:install` and `boost:update` regenerate them; the `.ai/rules` directory (project rules recorded by agents) should be committed.

Warning

Boost's MCP server can run database queries and code through Tinker, so the development `.env` must point at a local database and never at the shared server.

### Support windows[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/laravel.html#support-windows)

Laravel gives each major 18 months of bug fixes and two years of security fixes. From its release notes: 11 reached the end of security fixes on 2026-03-12; 12 (PHP 8.2 to 8.5) gets security fixes until 2027-02-24; 13 (PHP 8.3 to 8.5) until 2028-03-17. Name the major in the generator's tests, so a new release cannot change output unseen, and print the end-of-security date in the generated README. Laravel 13 needs PHP 8.3, which is also the stack's floor: 8.2 security support ends 2026-12-31.

### Trust the HA-Proxy, not every sender[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/laravel.html#trust-the-ha-proxy-not-every-sender)

Citadel ends TLS at HA-Proxy, so the app sees plain HTTP. Behind a balancer that ends TLS, Laravel's `url` helper can produce `http` links until `trustProxies` is set in `bootstrap/app.php`. The generated app should list the proxy addresses (from env) and also set `trustHosts`. Raw PHP gets the same behavior from HELMET.

### Work on the shared MySQL 5.6[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/laravel.html#work-on-the-shared-mysql-5-6)

Laravel's database docs list MySQL 5.7+ and MariaDB 10.3+ as supported; the shared server is MySQL 5.6, which left extended support on 2021-02-28. The practical limit is the index key prefix: 767 bytes for REDUNDANT and COMPACT tables, which is 191 characters in utf8mb4. Laravel's default string column is 255 characters, so a unique index on it can fail with error 1071. The Laravel templates set the 191 default with `Schema::defaultStringLength(191)` in `app/Providers/AppServiceProvider.php` and avoid JSON columns, so string columns stay inside the limit (PROCTOR `mysql56-string-default`). Sail's MySQL is current, so a developer's migrations can pass locally and fail on deploy.

### Next steps[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/laravel.html#next-steps)

Each Laravel bake prints Next steps suited to the shape. For `--laravel`:

```bash
composer install
cp .env.example .env
php artisan key:generate
php artisan migrate
php artisan serve
```

The islands and Inertia shapes add the front-end build between `migrate` and `serve`:

```bash
npm install
npm run build
```

The bake runs `php artisan migrate` after `php artisan key:generate`, so a freshly baked app has its database before the first request instead of answering 500 until someone migrates by hand.

### The Oracle check[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/laravel.html#the-oracle-check)

Oracle is wired but dormant in every generated app. The settings `ORACLE_USERNAME`, `ORACLE_PASSWORD`, and either `ORACLE_TNS` or `ORACLE_HOST`, `ORACLE_PORT`, `ORACLE_SERVICE_NAME` ship commented out in `.env.example`; while they are empty, nothing connects and nothing errors. Once you fill them in, Laravel apps check the wiring with:

```bash
php artisan oracle:check
```

The command finds the check file where it lives: `oracle-check.php` at the app root, where Squire's Laravel layout ships it, first, then `deploy/oracle-check.php`.

### Related[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/laravel.html#related)

- [Pick a shape](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/shapes.html)
- [The manifest](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/manifest.html)
- [Keeping apps current](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/keeping-current.html)
- [Every developer, every operating system](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/every-os.html)

## The manifest[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/manifest.html#the-manifest)

Every app Sourdough generates carries a `.sourdough/manifest.json`, the starter's memory of what went into the loaf. This page explains what it records and how to check your app against it; commit the manifest so a later `sourdough feed` can bring template updates in without clobbering what you have changed.

### What it records[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/manifest.html#what-it-records)

The manifest records the Sourdough version, the template, the answers you chose, and a sha256 hash of every file. Its keys, sorted alphabetically in the JSON:

| Key | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `answers` | each option you chose, sorted by key |
| `files` | every generated file with its `sha256` hash and a `class` of `managed` or `seeded` |
| `generated_at` | the generation time, UTC |
| `schema` | the manifest schema version, currently `1` |
| `sourdough_version` | the Sourdough package version, or `dev` when it cannot be determined (running from a git checkout without a release tag) |
| `template` | the template the app was generated from |

The JSON is pretty-printed with sorted keys and a trailing newline, and paths use forward slashes on every OS, so two runs with the same answers differ only in `generated_at`.

### Managed and seeded[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/manifest.html#managed-and-seeded)

| Class | Who owns it |
| --- | --- |
| `managed` | Sourdough owns the file and will update it |
| `seeded` | Sourdough wrote the file once; you own it now (`.env.example` and `README.md`) |

The manifest remembers what went into the loaf, so `feed` knows what to refresh and what to leave to rise on its own. A later `sourdough feed` reads it to bring template updates into your app without clobbering what you've changed.

### Check an app against its manifest[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/manifest.html#check-an-app-against-its-manifest)

Until `feed` ships, `sourdough manifest --check` is the gate. Run it in your app to list the managed files that have drifted from the manifest:

```bash
sourdough manifest --check
```

You can pass the app directory as an argument; the default is the current directory. The exit codes match PROCTOR:

- `0` clean: `Clean: every managed file matches the manifest.`
- `1` a managed file changed or is missing: one line per file, `changed <file>` or `missing <file>`
- `2` tool error: no manifest in the directory, or no `--check`

Seeded files are never reported. They're yours.

Tip

Commit `.sourdough/manifest.json` in your app. It's the record that keeps `feed` honest.

### The Squire deploy files[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/manifest.html#the-squire-deploy-files)

The deploy files in your app (`build.sh`, `scripts/release.sh`, the `.squire/` config, and their friends) come from Squire's exported copy, checked into this repository at `templates/squire/`. Squire owns them; Sourdough installs them as-is and records them in the manifest, so you never edit them by hand. To refresh them, run `composer squire-copy:sync`, which rewrites the copy from the installed `waynestate/squire` package, then verify it with `composer squire-copy:check` (part of `composer ci`).

### Related[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/manifest.html#related)

- [Pick a shape](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/shapes.html)
- [Describe a plan](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/describe-a-plan.html)

## Quick start[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html#quick-start)

From a machine where `sourdough` is installed (see [Install](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html)), bake an app and prove it.

### Steps[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html#steps)

1. Scaffold the app.
   ```
   sourdough new my-app
   ```
   Expected: exit code `0` (done). The `my-app` directory appears with a Wayne State app in it: SESAME (auth), HELMET (baseline runtime), PROCTOR (checks), and the Preflight CI components already wired in. Sourdough prints Next steps for the new app.
2. Run the app's own checks.
   From inside `my-app/`:
   ```
   composer ci
   ```
   Expected: exit code `0`. A freshly baked app passes its own `composer ci` on the first run.

### What you built[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html#what-you-built)

- A Wayne State app with the stack already wired in: SESAME (auth), HELMET (baseline runtime), PROCTOR (checks), and the Preflight CI components.
- Playbook wiring by default: the VCS repository, the package in `require`, `config.gitlab-domains` so Composer sends your token to git.wayne.edu, the seven setting names in `.env.example`, a `composer playbook` script that shows whether Playbook is installed, and a "WSU values (PLAYBOOK)" README section.
- ADVISOR in `require-dev`, a git-ignored `.mcp.json`, and an "ADVISOR" README section.
- `.sourdough/manifest.json`, the starter's memory: the Sourdough version, the template, the answers you chose, and a sha256 hash of every file, each marked `managed` (Sourdough owns it and will update it) or `seeded` (Sourdough wrote it once and you own it now: `.env.example` and `README.md`).

### Next steps[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html#next-steps)

- Follow the app's printed Next steps: they point at `composer playbook` once dependencies are in, and at `php vendor/bin/advisor install --client=claude --write` for ADVISOR.
- [Pick a shape](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/shapes.html): the permutations, from raw PHP to Laravel plus Inertia/Vue.
- [Describe a plan](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/describe-a-plan.html): describe what the app does and let a model plan it.
- [The manifest](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/manifest.html): what the manifest records, and `sourdough manifest --check`.
- [CI](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/ci.html): set up the generated app's CI; a git.wayne.edu instance runner is strongly recommended.
- [Commands](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html): every flag and option.

---

Source: https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/shapes.html

## Pick a shape[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/shapes.html#pick-a-shape)

A starter in a jar is only potential until you give it a shape: pick the permutation below, then run `sourdough new` with the matching flags. If you would rather describe the app in a sentence and let a model plan it, continue to [Describe a plan](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/describe-a-plan.html).

![Five loaves on the proofing bench (raw, raw + vue, blade, blade + islands, inertia) above the feeding schedule chalkboard](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/readme/gallery.jpg)

### The five permutations[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/shapes.html#the-five-permutations)

| Flags | Permutation |
| --- | --- |
| (none) or `--raw` | Raw PHP with WayneUI's standalone path |
| `--raw --vue` | Raw PHP + Vue SPA over JSON |
| `--laravel` | Laravel + Blade |
| `--laravel --vue` | Laravel + Blade + Vue islands |
| `--laravel --inertia` (or `--inertia`) | Laravel + Inertia/Vue |

All five permutations generate in 0.1. `--raw --vue` is the raw PHP bake with a Vue 3 front end over it: PHP answers JSON under `/api/`, Vite builds the Vue app, and `src/Vite.php` loads it from the build or the dev server.

Run `sourdough new` with the flags for the row you want. `dir` is the directory to create the app in:

raw

```bash
sourdough new my-app --raw
```

raw + vue

```bash
sourdough new my-app --raw --vue
```

laravel

```bash
sourdough new my-app --laravel
```

laravel + vue

```bash
sourdough new my-app --laravel --vue
```

inertia

```bash
sourdough new my-app --inertia
```

### The template directories[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/shapes.html#the-template-directories)

Each shape bakes from a directory in `templates/`:

| Template directory | Shape |
| --- | --- |
| `raw/` | Raw PHP with WayneUI's standalone path |
| `raw-vue/` | Raw PHP + Vue SPA over JSON (copied over `raw/`) |
| `laravel-blade/` | Laravel + Blade |
| `laravel-blade-vue/` | Laravel + Blade + Vue islands |
| `laravel-inertia/` | Laravel + Inertia/Vue |

`squire/` holds Squire's exported deploy files. Squire owns them; Sourdough installs them as-is into every app and records them in the manifest, so you never edit them by hand.

The raw template also carries its own checks:

- Pinstripe's coding standard: `pint.json` (the per preset, with the fetched `public/wayne-ui.php` kept out and `vendor` excluded) and `phpstan.neon` (Pinstripe's raw preset, level 8 over `src/` and `public/`), with `waynestate/pinstripe` in require-dev and the extension-installer plugin allowed, and `lint`, `fix` and `analyse` scripts, so `composer ci` runs test, lint, analyse, proctor and audit in that order.
- An explicit `composer-ci` job in `.gitlab-ci.yml` (`composer install`, then `composer ci`), mirroring the Laravel overlay, so PROCTOR sees a `composer ci` in the pipeline instead of warning that no job runs it.
- `stubs/wayne-ui.php`, a static-analysis stub for the run-time WayneUI functions (`wsu_shell_start`, `wsu_shell_end`) that `phpstan.neon` scans through `scanFiles`.
- A front controller that answers `404` for any path but `/` (a short not-found page that keeps WayneUI's layout and links home) instead of rendering the home page for every URL; `/up` stays HELMET's and answers first.

### Raw PHP + Vue[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/shapes.html#raw-php-vue)

`--raw --vue` keeps everything above and swaps the page for a Vue 3 app. PHP boots HELMET, the session and SESAME the same way, then answers JSON under `/api/` (`/api/me` is the signed-in user) and sends one page that loads the Vue app. WayneUI comes from its Vue package and its layered dist stylesheet, pinned as in the Inertia shape, so there is no `public/wayne-ui.php` to fetch. Run it with:

```bash
composer install
npm install
npm run build
composer serve
```

Run `npm run dev` in a second terminal for hot reload: `src/Vite.php` loads the app from the dev server while it runs, and from `public/build` otherwise. See [Templates](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/templates.html#raw-vue) for every file it adds.

### Oracle in every shape[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/shapes.html#oracle-in-every-shape)

Oracle is wired but dormant in every generated app. The settings `ORACLE_USERNAME`, `ORACLE_PASSWORD`, and either `ORACLE_TNS` or `ORACLE_HOST`, `ORACLE_PORT`, `ORACLE_SERVICE_NAME` ship commented out in `.env.example`; while they are empty, nothing connects and nothing errors. Once you fill them in, Laravel apps check the wiring with `php artisan oracle:check`, and raw PHP apps run queries through the `App\Oracle` helper, which takes values only as binds and answers mistakes with plain sentences. The command finds the check file where it lives: `oracle-check.php` at the app root, where Squire's Laravel layout ships it, first, then `deploy/oracle-check.php`.

### Related[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/shapes.html#related)

- [Describe a plan](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/describe-a-plan.html)
- [The manifest](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/manifest.html)

Source: https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/testing.html

## Testing[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/testing.html#testing)

This page is the proofing bench: how to run Sourdough's own checks day to day, and how to fire the smoke gate that bakes a shape for real before it may be claimed. Like any starter, Sourdough needs regular feeding, or it goes flat. For the wider runbook, continue to [Maintaining](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/maintaining.html).

Note

Maintainers: how to build, test and release this project, and where its data comes from, is in [MAINTAINING.md](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/maintaining.html).

### Day-to-day commands[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/testing.html#day-to-day-commands)

| Task | Command |
| --- | --- |
| Install | `composer install` |
| All checks (what CI runs) | `composer ci` |
| Only the tests | `composer test` |
| Fix code style | `composer fix` |
| Check the Squire copy | `composer squire-copy:check` |
| Refresh the Squire copy | `composer squire-copy:sync`, then commit `templates/squire/` |
| Try a generation | `php bin/sourdough new ./demo --raw --dry-run` |

`composer ci` runs `composer validate --strict`, the tests, Pint, PHPStan, the Squire copy check, the agent-ready files check, the docs site check and `composer audit`.

### With only Docker[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/testing.html#with-only-docker)

The same lines work in PowerShell and sh:

```
docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/app" -w /app composer:2.10.3 sh -c "composer install --no-interaction && composer ci"
docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/app" -w /app php:8.5-cli vendor/bin/phpunit
```

### From the repo root[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/testing.html#from-the-repo-root)

```
docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/app" -w /app composer:2 composer install --no-interaction
docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/app" -w /app php:8.3-cli vendor/bin/phpunit
docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/app" -w /app php:8.4-cli vendor/bin/phpunit
docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/app" -w /app composer:2 composer validate --strict
docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/app" -w /app php:8.4-cli php bin/sourdough new /tmp/demo --dry-run
```

### The smoke gate[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/testing.html#the-smoke-gate)

The smoke gate is the proofing bench: it proofs one shape at a time before that shape may be claimed. It bakes the app with this checkout's own `bin/sourdough new <dir> --no-advisor --no-input` (the CLI under test is the one being shipped), then runs the generated app's own checks:

- `raw`: `composer install` and `composer ci`
- `raw-vue`: the raw steps plus `npm install` and `npm run build`, then a live server that must answer `/` with the built app, `/api/me` with the signed-in user (and `401` without a session), `/nope` with `404` and `/up` with `200`
- `blade`: the raw steps plus `cp .env.example .env`, `php artisan key:generate`, `php artisan migrate` and `php artisan test`
- `blade-vue`: the blade steps plus `npm install` and `npm run build`
- `inertia`: the blade steps plus `npm install`, `npm run build` and `npm run typecheck`

Each step prints `ok`; the first `FAIL` stops the run and shows the command's tail. A shape is claimed in the docs only when its smoke is green.

Run it per OS. The image (`scripts/smoke.Dockerfile`) pins php 8.5, composer 2 and node 22, so the bake is identical everywhere:

linux

```bash
docker build -f scripts/smoke.Dockerfile -t sourdough-smoke:local .
docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/repo:ro" -v /work -e SMOKE_WORK=/work sourdough-smoke:local sh /repo/scripts/smoke-shape.sh <shape>
```

windows

```powershell
.\scripts\smoke-shape.ps1 <shape>
```

The PowerShell wrapper builds the same image once and reuses it. Pass `-WorkDir <dir>` to bind a local folder to `/work` so the scratch copy, the generated app and the per-step logs survive the run. On Windows, `.\scripts\smoke-shape.ps1 <shape>` runs it in one line.

Two environment variables control the scratch space:

- `SMOKE_WORK`: the scratch dir for the copy, the app and the logs. Defaults to a fresh temp dir that is removed on exit.
- `SMOKE_KEEP`: set to `1` to keep the scratch dir behind for inspection.

Note

On CI the gate runs as one job per shape: `smoke` (matrix) on GitHub, `smoke-raw`, `smoke-raw-vue`, `smoke-blade`, `smoke-blade-vue` and `smoke-inertia` on GitLab. All are `allow_failure: true` until the lead has seen every shape green on CI once; flip them to blocking after that proof.

### Related[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/testing.html#related)

- [CI](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/ci.html)
- [Pick a shape](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/shapes.html)
- [Same kitchen, many ovens](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/ovens.html)
- [Maintaining](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/maintaining.html)

## Wiring the stack in[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/wiring-the-stack.html#wiring-the-stack-in)

Goal: know exactly what Sourdough wires into a freshly baked app, and why each piece is a default rather than an option. Read this before your first bake, and keep it at hand while you maintain an app. Like the starter it is named after, a Sourdough app only stays alive while something keeps feeding it; the wiring below is the first meal.

Sourdough is the app starter for the WSU stack. One command scaffolds a new app with SESAME (auth), HELMET (baseline runtime), PROCTOR (checks), and the Preflight CI components already in place. It is one PHP command, so it works on Windows, macOS, and Linux.

![The proof: dough rises past its gold band as WayneUI, SESAME, HELMET, PROCTOR and Preflight go in one by one, over the feeding schedule](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/readme/proof.svg)

*The proofing log from the front page: what goes into the tub when you run `sourdough new`, and the day-to-day check that keeps it alive.*

### What lands in every app[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/wiring-the-stack.html#what-lands-in-every-app)

Every generated app has SESAME, HELMET, PROCTOR as a dev dependency, a `.gitlab-ci.yml` that includes the Preflight components, a `/up` route that does not touch the database, and a README that points at the CREED handbook. The libraries are tagged (SESAME, HELMET with a health check, PROCTOR, Preflight templates), and `sourdough new` wires them into every generated app.

Defaults decide what most apps end up doing, so the stack is wired in by default, not as an option. Laravel's own kits include sign-in, rate limiting and two-factor login out of the box for the same reason.

For the Playbook and ADVISOR wiring and the flags that turn each one off, see [Commands](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html).

### The release script runs the check, but do not call it the gate[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/wiring-the-stack.html#the-release-script-runs-the-check-but-do-not-call-it-the-gate)

The Citadel release script runs `proctor check` and stops on exit 1. Treat that as a report. A failure in a release script cannot stop bad code from going live on a Quick Update, so the real gates are CI before merge and, later, a platform check.

Warning

Promising a gate that does not hold is worse than having none. Nothing prevents someone from describing the script as a gate in a README.

### Keep the start-up path small and boring[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/wiring-the-stack.html#keep-the-start-up-path-small-and-boring)

Generated commands should run and exit on their own, with no prompts and no network calls after install. Developers, CI and coding agents all run them, and a prompt that waits for input breaks all three.

### Accessibility gate[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/wiring-the-stack.html#accessibility-gate)

The US Justice Department's Title II web rule sets WCAG 2.1 Level AA for state and local government web content. An interim final rule published on 2026-04-20 moved the first compliance date to 2027-04-26 for entities of 50,000 people or more and to 2028-04-26 for smaller ones. The standard and the ongoing duty to keep content accessible did not change. Whether and when the rule applies to a given WSU app is not decided here; ask WSU's accessibility office.

For Sourdough: each permutation's generated home page and sign-in flow get an automated accessibility check in CI, including the Vue paths (focus after navigation, announced route changes); WayneUI's accessible templates are the default markup; and the "new app" page passes the same gate.

Note

Automated checks find only part of the problems, so the generated README should say so.

### Protect deploy credentials in the generated pipeline[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/wiring-the-stack.html#protect-deploy-credentials-in-the-generated-pipeline)

GitLab's docs say masking a variable does not reliably stop a malicious user from reading it; protected variables exist only in pipelines on protected branches and tags; a pipeline for a merge request from a fork should run in the parent project only after review, because malicious code can compromise masked and protected variables; and sensitive values belong in an external secrets manager. A project's job-token allowlist includes only the project itself by default, and GitLab calls disabling it a security risk. From GitLab 19.0 job tokens use the JWT format by default, and the legacy format is available only until 20.0. Which GitLab version WSU runs was not checked.

The generated `.gitlab-ci.yml` should therefore:

- run deploy jobs only on a protected branch or tag with protected variables
- put no secrets in component `inputs`
- leave the job-token allowlist on
- add other projects to it by name when the pipeline must fetch from them

Danger

Sensitive values belong in an external secrets manager. Put no secrets in component `inputs`, and run deploy jobs only on a protected branch or tag with protected variables.

### Where the code lives[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/wiring-the-stack.html#where-the-code-lives)

The canonical repository is on nougat: [enterprise-apps/sourdough](https://nougat.snu.gs/enterprise-apps/sourdough). git.wayne.edu and GitHub ([waynestate/sourdough](https://github.com/waynestate/sourdough)) are read-only mirrors of it. Open issues and merge requests on nougat, not on the mirrors. This moves to git.wayne.edu once it has CI runners. Nougat is the starter culture; the mirrors are just slices.

### Related[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/wiring-the-stack.html#related)

- [Commands](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html)
- [Plan format](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/plan-format.html)

---

Source: https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/

## Sourdough[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/#sourdough)

![php](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/readme/badges/php.svg) ![license](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/readme/badges/license.svg) ![exit codes](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/readme/badges/exit-codes.svg) [![GitHub CI](https://github.com/waynestate/sourdough/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/waynestate/sourdough/actions/workflows/ci.yml)

**Feed it and it grows.**

A starter you feed: `sourdough new` makes a Wayne State app with the stack already wired in. One command scaffolds a new app with SESAME (auth), HELMET (baseline runtime), Pinstripe (coding standard), PROCTOR (checks), and the Preflight CI components already in place. It is one PHP command, so it works on Windows, macOS, and Linux.

Every loaf gets proofed before it ships. Checks: `composer ci` (the same command runs on GitLab and GitHub).

![The proof: dough rises past its gold band as WayneUI, SESAME, HELMET, PROCTOR and Preflight go in one by one, over the feeding schedule](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/readme/proof.svg)

The proofing log from the front page: what goes into the tub when you run `sourdough new`, and the day-to-day check that keeps it alive.

### Install[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/#install)

```
composer global require waynestate/sourdough
```

After `composer global require`, the `sourdough` command lives in `composer global config bin-dir --absolute`; put that directory on your PATH. Or scaffold without installing, with `composer create-project waynestate/sourdough`. The full instructions are on [Install](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html).

### First run[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/#first-run)

```
sourdough new my-app
```

Expected: exit code `0` (done), a `my-app` directory holding a Wayne State app with the stack wired in, and Next steps printed for it. Then run the app's own gate from inside `my-app/`:

```
composer ci
```

The step-by-step version is the [Quick start](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html).

### Pick your path[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/#pick-your-path)

- [Quick start](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html): bake your first app and run its checks.
- [Install](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html): what the machine needs, and the two ways to get Sourdough.
- [Reference](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html): every command and option, the plan format, the templates.

### Status[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/#status)

Version 0.1.5 (2026-11-03), MIT license. Agents: this site ships [llms.txt](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/llms.txt) for LLM readers.

## Install[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html#install)

Sourdough is one PHP command, so it works on Windows, macOS, and Linux.

### Requirements[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html#requirements)

- PHP 8.3 or newer (`^8.3` in `composer.json`).
- Composer, for the install lines below.
- No PHP extensions are declared in `composer.json`.

Where the code lives: the canonical repository is on nougat: [enterprise-apps/sourdough](https://nougat.snu.gs/enterprise-apps/sourdough). git.wayne.edu and GitHub ([waynestate/sourdough](https://github.com/waynestate/sourdough)) are read-only mirrors of it. Open issues and merge requests on nougat, not on the mirrors. Nougat is the starter culture; the mirrors are just slices.

### Install[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html#install-1)

Two ways in: install the `sourdough` command on your machine, or scaffold without installing.

composer global require

```bash
composer global require waynestate/sourdough
```

composer create-project

```bash
composer create-project waynestate/sourdough
```

Note

After `composer global require`, the `sourdough` command lives in `composer global config bin-dir --absolute`; put that directory on your PATH.

### Verify[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html#verify)

```bash
sourdough --version
```

Expected:

```
Sourdough 0.1.5
```

The CLI is a Symfony Console application named Sourdough, version 0.1.5 (`bin/sourdough`), so `--version` prints the name and the version.

## MAINTAINING: feeding the starter[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/maintaining.html#maintaining-feeding-the-starter)

How to build, test, release and keep Sourdough alive. Sourdough makes a Wayne State app with the stack already wired in and is meant to own that wiring for the app's whole life. Built today: `new` and `new --describe`, plus `manifest`. Planned: `adopt` and `feed`. Like any starter, it needs regular feeding, or it goes flat.

### What Sourdough is and what it depends on[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/maintaining.html#what-sourdough-is-and-what-it-depends-on)

- `waynestate/sourdough` on Packagist, with the CLI `bin/sourdough`.
- Runtime dependencies: `symfony/console`, `symfony/http-client`, `justinrainbow/json-schema`, `openai-php/client` (only for `new --describe`, which can ask an OpenAI-compatible model for a plan; optional). No other stack package at runtime.
- **Generated apps** require `waynestate/helmet`, `waynestate/sesame` and `waynestate/proctor` from Packagist.
- **It carries a copy of Squire's templates** in `templates/squire/` (`raw/`, `laravel/`, `static/`, `vue/`, `catalog.json`, `manifest.json`). Squire owns those files; Sourdough never hand-edits them. `composer squire-copy:sync` rewrites the copy from the installed `waynestate/squire` package (dev dependency `^0.4`), and `composer squire-copy:check` (part of `composer ci`) exits 1 when the committed copy has drifted.
- The planned `feed` will need only git on the developer's machine: it records the template commit an app came from and applies template changes with `git apply --3way`.

### Where it lives[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/maintaining.html#where-it-lives)

Development happens on nougat, the canonical repository ([enterprise-apps/sourdough](https://nougat.snu.gs/enterprise-apps/sourdough)). This GitHub repository and git.wayne.edu are read-only mirrors: `main` and tags are copied automatically. Changes, issues and merge requests go to nougat. Nobody pushes to the mirrors.

### Build and test[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/maintaining.html#build-and-test)

| Task | Command |
| --- | --- |
| Install | `composer install` |
| All checks (what CI runs) | `composer ci` |
| Only the tests | `composer test` |
| Fix code style | `composer fix` |
| Check the Squire copy | `composer squire-copy:check` |
| Refresh the Squire copy | `composer squire-copy:sync`, then commit `templates/squire/` |
| Try a generation | `php bin/sourdough new ./demo --raw --dry-run` |

With only Docker (the same lines work in PowerShell and sh):

```
docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/app" -w /app composer:2.10.3 sh -c "composer install --no-interaction && composer ci"
docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/app" -w /app php:8.5-cli vendor/bin/phpunit
```

`composer ci` runs `composer validate --strict`, the tests, Pint, PHPStan, the Squire copy check, the agent-ready files check, the docs site check and `composer audit`.

### CI[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/maintaining.html#ci)

- **GitLab:** Preflight's `php-test` (PHP 8.3, 8.4, 8.5) and `composer-audit` components, plus a `composer-ci` job.
- **GitHub:** `.github/workflows/ci.yml` calls Preflight's reusable workflow with `composer ci`.
- Green means `composer ci` passed on all three PHP versions on both.

### Smoke gate[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/maintaining.html#smoke-gate)

The smoke gate is the proofing bench: it proofs one shape at a time before that shape may be claimed. It bakes the app with this checkout's own `bin/sourdough new <dir> --no-advisor --no-input` (the CLI under test is the one being shipped), then runs the generated app's own checks:

- `raw`: `composer install` and `composer ci`
- `raw-vue`: the raw steps plus `npm install` and `npm run build`, then a live server that must answer `/` with the built app, `/api/me` with the signed-in user (and `401` without a session), `/nope` with `404` and `/up` with `200`
- `blade`: the raw steps plus `cp .env.example .env`, `php artisan key:generate`, `php artisan migrate` and `php artisan test`
- `blade-vue`: the blade steps plus `npm install` and `npm run build`
- `inertia`: the blade steps plus `npm install`, `npm run build` and `npm run typecheck`

Each step prints `ok`; the first `FAIL` stops the run and shows the command's tail. A shape is claimed in the docs only when its smoke is green.

Run it per OS. The image (`scripts/smoke.Dockerfile`) pins php 8.5, composer 2 and node 22, so the bake is identical everywhere:

Linux and macOS:

```
docker build -f scripts/smoke.Dockerfile -t sourdough-smoke:local .
docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/repo:ro" -v /work -e SMOKE_WORK=/work sourdough-smoke:local sh /repo/scripts/smoke-shape.sh <shape>
```

Windows PowerShell:

```
.\scripts\smoke-shape.ps1 <shape>
```

The PowerShell wrapper builds the same image once and reuses it. Pass `-WorkDir <dir>` to bind a local folder to `/work` so the scratch copy, the generated app and the per-step logs survive the run.

Two environment variables control the scratch space:

- `SMOKE_WORK`: the scratch dir for the copy, the app and the logs. Defaults to a fresh temp dir that is removed on exit.
- `SMOKE_KEEP`: set to `1` to keep the scratch dir behind for inspection.

On CI the gate runs as one job per shape: `smoke` (matrix) on GitHub, `smoke-raw`, `smoke-raw-vue`, `smoke-blade`, `smoke-blade-vue` and `smoke-inertia` on GitLab. All are `allow_failure: true` until the lead has seen every shape green on CI once; flip them to blocking after that proof.

### Refreshing the Squire templates[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/maintaining.html#refreshing-the-squire-templates)

When Squire's templates change, regenerate the copy from a Squire checkout, then verify it:

```
php ../squire/bin/export-templates.php --to=../sourdough/templates/squire
php ../squire/bin/export-templates.php --to=../sourdough/templates/squire --check
```

Commit the refreshed copy with the Squire commit in the message, and add a CHANGELOG line. Until `feed` exists, apps generated earlier pick up template changes by hand.

### What belongs here[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/maintaining.html#what-belongs-here)

If every app should have something, it goes in Sourdough's templates. If only the Laravel + Inertia/Vue shape (WELD) should have it, it lives in WELD. Version rules belong to CREED, checks to PROCTOR, Citadel scripts to Squire.

### Releasing[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/maintaining.html#releasing)

1. Move the lines under `## Unreleased` in `CHANGELOG.md` to a new `## X.Y.Z (YYYY-MM-DD)` heading.
2. `composer ci` and the Squire copy check green locally, then both pipelines green for that commit.
3. Run a secrets scan of the history and check that nothing internal (server names, people, IDs) is in the tree.
4. Tag `X.Y.Z` (no `v`) on nougat. The mirror carries the tag to GitHub, and Packagist picks it up from there.
5. A release needs a maintainer's approval. Never move or delete a published tag.

### The front page[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/maintaining.html#the-front-page)

`site/` is the static front page, for `https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/` on Citadel, served through a small raw-PHP `deploy/` layer generated with Squire.

### Things that trip people up[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/maintaining.html#things-that-trip-people-up)

- In 0.1 all five shapes generate. `--raw --vue` apps need `npm run build` (or `npm run dev`) before `/` renders: `src/Vite.php` refuses with a plain message when there is neither a build nor a dev server.
- Commit `.sourdough/manifest.json` in generated apps; the planned `feed` will need it.

### Who maintains it[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/maintaining.html#who-maintains-it)

Adam Perkins, Wayne State University Enterprise Applications. Internal runbook (accounts, tokens, mirrors, deploy access): ask Enterprise Applications.

Source: https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html

## Commands[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html#commands)

Reference for the `sourdough` CLI: every command, argument, option and exit code, exactly as the sources define them. For the JSON plan behind `--describe` and `--plan`, see [Plan format](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/plan-format.html).

### sourdough new[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html#sourdough-new)

Make a new Wayne State app with the stack already wired in.

```
sourdough new [dir] [options]
```

`dir` is the directory to create the app in. It is required unless you use `--describe`.

#### Options[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html#options)

| Option | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--raw` | use the raw PHP base |
| `--laravel` | use the Laravel base |
| `--vue` | add a Vue front end |
| `--inertia` | use Inertia/Vue (implies `--laravel`) |
| `--sail` | run the Laravel app on Sail for local work (compose.yaml; needs WSL2 on Windows) |
| `--docker` | generate a Dockerfile and compose.yaml for local work (native on every OS; amd64 and arm64) |
| `--dry-run` | print the plan and write nothing |
| `--name` | app name (default: the basename of `<dir>`) |
| `--no-input` | never prompt (Sourdough 0.1 has no prompts) |
| `--json` | with `--dry-run`, print the plan as JSON |
| `--describe "<sentence>"` | describe what the app does; a model plans it (needs the `SOURDOUGH_LLM_*` env vars) |
| `--plan-only` | with `--describe`, print the plan as JSON and write nothing |
| `--plan <file>` | a ready-made plan file (JSON matching `resources/plan.schema.json`) |
| `--playbook` | kept for compatibility: Playbook is now the default |
| `--no-playbook` | skip the Playbook wiring (for CI and automated tests only; WSU apps need Playbook) |
| `--no-advisor` | skip the ADVISOR wiring (no `require-dev` entry, no `.mcp.json` git-ignore, no README section) |

Note

`--sail` and `--docker` are both real for the Laravel shapes (`--laravel`, `--laravel --vue` and `--inertia`) and mutually exclusive: together they are refused with `Choose one of --sail or --docker, not both.` (exit `1`). With `--sail` the app runs on Laravel Sail: `laravel/sail` in require-dev, a `compose.yaml`, the database settings in `.env.example` and a README section; the database is MySQL 8.4 LTS. On Windows, Sail needs WSL2, and `--docker` is the route that works natively. With `--docker` Sourdough writes the app's own Docker setup after the shape is baked: a two-target `Dockerfile` (dev and prod) whose base images are pinned by manifest-list digest, a `compose.yaml` with a MySQL 8.4 service (and a vite service for the Vue and Inertia shapes), a `.dockerignore`, the PHP ini files the image copies in, the `composer dev-up`, `dev-down` and `dev-shell` scripts, the database settings in `.env.example`, and a "Run it locally with Docker" README section. It works natively on Windows, macOS and Linux (no WSL2 needed) and is checked on amd64 and arm64. Playbook credentials reach a production build only as a BuildKit secret, never a build arg. The raw paths keep their own refusal at the plan step: "`--sail` and `--docker` are for the Laravel paths: the raw paths run on plain PHP."

#### Exit codes[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html#exit-codes)

Exit codes: `0` done, `1` refused (invalid flags, non-empty target, not available, model gave up), `2` tool error.

| Refused case | Exact message | Exit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--describe` and `--plan` together | `--describe and --plan are mutually exclusive.` | `1` |
| `--sail` and `--docker` together | `Choose one of --sail or --docker, not both.` | `1` |
| `--sail` or `--docker` with a raw permutation | `--sail and --docker are for the Laravel paths: the raw paths run on plain PHP.` | `1` |
| `--playbook` and `--no-playbook` together | `--playbook and --no-playbook are mutually exclusive.` | `1` |
| `--plan-only` without `--describe` | `--plan-only is only available with --describe.` | `1` |
| `dir` missing without `--describe` | `The dir argument is required unless you use --describe.` | `1` |
| no read access to Playbook | `You need read access to Playbook (a private package on git.wayne.edu) to make a Wayne State app.` plus the how-to | `1` |
| `--json` without `--dry-run` | `--json is only available with --dry-run.` | `2` |
| the model could not be reached (`--describe`) | `The model could not be reached:` plus the underlying error | `2` |

Other refusals, all exit `1`: invalid flags, a non-empty target, a model that gives up (the message points to `--plan=<file>`), and an app name that fails validation.

#### Playbook access check[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html#playbook-access-check)

By default the generated app requires `waynestate/playbook` (WSU's private shared-values package on git.wayne.edu): the VCS repository, the package in `require`, `config.gitlab-domains` so Composer sends your token to git.wayne.edu, the seven setting names in `.env.example`, a `composer playbook` script that shows whether Playbook is installed, and a "WSU values (PLAYBOOK)" README section that explains how to get read access.

Before writing anything, `sourdough new` checks that this machine can read the package (a Composer credential, then a direct git probe):

| Situation | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| no read access | refuses with exit `1` and prints the how-to |
| git.wayne.edu unreachable | still generates the app, but warns that `composer install` will need the connection |
| non-interactive run or CI environment | skips the check |
| `--dry-run` | runs the check but never refuses; the JSON plan carries a `playbook` key with the mode, the access status and the probe that answered |

After generation the Next steps point at `composer playbook`. `--playbook` is kept for compatibility and changes nothing; `--no-playbook` skips all of it. The two flags together are refused with exit `1`.

#### ADVISOR wiring[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html#advisor-wiring)

Generated apps ship with ADVISOR wired in by default: `waynestate/advisor` lands in `require-dev`, `.mcp.json` is git-ignored (a client config starts a program for whoever opens the project), and the README gains an "ADVISOR" section. The Next steps print the install line once dependencies are in:

```
php vendor/bin/advisor install --client=claude --write
```

`--no-advisor` skips all of it.

#### App name validation[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html#app-name-validation)

The app name (from `--name`, from the plan, or from the basename of `<dir>`) must start with a letter or number and use only letters, numbers, spaces, dots, dashes and underscores, at most 63 characters; anything else is refused before anything is written.

#### Next steps printed after generation[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html#next-steps-printed-after-generation)

| Shape | Steps |
| --- | --- |
| Raw PHP | `cd <dir>`, `composer install`, `composer serve` |
| Laravel + Blade | `cd <dir>`, `composer install`, `cp .env.example .env`, `php artisan key:generate`, `php artisan migrate`, `php artisan serve` |
| Laravel + Blade + Vue islands | the Laravel + Blade steps plus `npm install` and `npm run build` |
| Laravel + Inertia/Vue | the Laravel + Blade steps plus `npm install` and `npm run build` |
| any Laravel shape with `--sail` | `cd <dir>`, `composer install`, `cp .env.example .env`, `./vendor/bin/sail up -d`, `./vendor/bin/sail artisan key:generate`, `./vendor/bin/sail artisan migrate`, `(Windows: run sail from WSL2, or use --docker)`; the Vue and Inertia shapes add `./vendor/bin/sail npm install` and `./vendor/bin/sail npm run dev` |
| any Laravel shape with `--docker` | `cd <dir>`, `composer install`, `cp .env.example .env`, `composer dev-up`, `docker compose exec app php artisan key:generate`, `docker compose exec app php artisan migrate`; the Vue and Inertia shapes end with `(Vite runs as its own service on port 5173)` |

With ADVISOR wired in, `php vendor/bin/advisor install --client=claude --write` is printed after `composer install`. With Playbook required, the output ends with: `WSU values: Playbook installs with composer install. Check it any time with: composer playbook`.

### sourdough manifest[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html#sourdough-manifest)

Check a generated app against its Sourdough manifest.

```
sourdough manifest [dir] [--check]
```

| Argument or option | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `dir` | the app directory to check (default: the current directory) |
| `--check` | list managed files that changed or are missing; exit 1 when anything changed |

Without `--check` the command answers "Use `sourdough manifest --check` to check the app against its manifest." and exits `2`.

Exit codes: `0` clean, `1` changed or missing, `2` tool error.

| Output | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `Clean: every managed file matches the manifest.` | every managed file matches the manifest |
| `changed <file>` | a managed file changed |
| `missing <file>` | a managed file is missing |

Seeded files are never reported: the app owns them.

### Related[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html#related)

- [Plan format](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/plan-format.html)
- [Wiring the stack in](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/wiring-the-stack.html)

---

Source: https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/plan-format.html

## Plan format[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/plan-format.html#plan-format)

Reference for the JSON plan that `sourdough new --describe` asks a model for and `sourdough new --plan <file>` reads back. Every plan is validated against `resources/plan.schema.json`. For the flags that produce a plan, see [Commands](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html).

### The plan object[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/plan-format.html#the-plan-object)

A plan is a small JSON object:

```json
{
    "permutation": "raw",
    "parts": ["sesame", "helmet"],
    "name": "my-app",
    "models": [
        {
            "name": "Post",
            "fields": [
                { "name": "title", "type": "string" },
                { "name": "body", "type": "text" }
            ]
        }
    ],
    "pages": ["/", "/posts"]
}
```

`permutation`, `parts`, and `name` are required; `models` and `pages` are optional.

| Key | Required | Values |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `permutation` | yes | one of the five permutation values below |
| `parts` | yes | a subset of `sesame`, `helmet`, `proctor`, and `preflight` |
| `name` | yes | the app name |
| `models` | no | a list of model objects |
| `pages` | no | a list of page paths, such as `/` and `/posts` |

When a plan is printed as JSON, empty `models` and `pages` are omitted.

#### Permutation values[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/plan-format.html#permutation-values)

| Value | Flags | Name |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `raw` | (none) or `--raw` | Raw PHP with WayneUI's standalone path |
| `raw-vue` | `--raw --vue` | Raw PHP + Vue SPA over JSON |
| `laravel-blade` | `--laravel` | Laravel + Blade |
| `laravel-blade-vue` | `--laravel --vue` | Laravel + Blade + Vue islands |
| `laravel-inertia` | `--laravel --inertia` (or `--inertia`) | Laravel + Inertia/Vue |

Flag resolution, from `src/Permutation.php`:

- `--inertia` implies `--laravel`: Inertia here means Laravel.
- `--raw` and `--laravel` are mutually exclusive: pick one base.
- `--vue` is not needed with `--inertia`: Inertia already means Vue.
- Combinations that make no sense are refused with an error that names the five shapes and their flags.

In 0.1 all five permutations generate.

#### Parts[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/plan-format.html#parts)

From `src/Part.php`, the stack parts a Sourdough app is wired with:

| Value | Part |
| --- | --- |
| `sesame` | SESAME (auth) |
| `helmet` | HELMET (baseline runtime) |
| `proctor` | PROCTOR (checks) |
| `preflight` | the Preflight CI components |

A plan's `parts` is a subset of these.

#### Models[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/plan-format.html#models)

Each model object has a `name` and a `fields` list; each field has a `name` and a `type`, both strings, as in the example above.

#### Pages[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/plan-format.html#pages)

A list of strings, such as `["/", "/posts"]`.

### Getting a plan[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/plan-format.html#getting-a-plan)

Instead of choosing flags, describe what the app does and let a model plan it:

```
sourdough new --describe "A blog with posts and comments"
```

Sourdough asks an OpenAI-compatible model for a plan, validates it against `resources/plan.schema.json`, and prints it. The model kneads the dough, but you decide when the loaf is ready to bake: if the answer is not valid JSON, does not match the schema, or the model gives up after one retry, Sourdough refuses with a message pointing you to `--plan=<file>` (exit `1`). You write the plan yourself and pass it in.

To see the plan as JSON without writing anything:

```
sourdough new --describe "A blog with posts and comments" --plan-only
```

Generation from a plan is not built yet in 0.1. Save the plan to a file and pass it with `--plan`:

```
sourdough new my-app --plan plan.json
```

`--plan` reads the file, validates it against the schema, and continues the normal generation flow using the plan's permutation and name.

#### Model configuration[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/plan-format.html#model-configuration)

`--describe` needs three environment variables (no defaults, no key in code):

| Variable | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `SOURDOUGH_LLM_BASE_URL` | the OpenAI-compatible endpoint, including the API path (usually `/v1`) |
| `SOURDOUGH_LLM_API_KEY` | the API key |
| `SOURDOUGH_LLM_MODEL` | the model name |

Any OpenAI-compatible endpoint works: a hosted API, a local server, or WarriorGPT. Sourdough does not care about the hostname; it only needs the base URL, key, and model.

Danger

`SOURDOUGH_LLM_API_KEY` is a secret. It has no default, and there is no key in code: set it in the environment for the run.

### The steps plan[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/plan-format.html#the-steps-plan)

The app plan is the what: permutation, parts, name, models, pages. The steps plan in `src/Plan.php` is the how, that is, what `sourdough new` will do, and `--dry-run` prints it. It carries the permutation, the target dir, and a list of steps:

| Condition | Step |
| --- | --- |
| raw permutation | `Copy the raw template into <dir>` |
| raw permutation | `Replace {{app_name}} and {{app_slug}} in file names and contents` |
| raw-vue permutation | `Copy the raw template, then the raw-vue template over it, into <dir>` |
| raw-vue permutation | `Replace {{app_name}} and {{app_slug}} in file names and contents` |
| any Laravel permutation | `Create the <label> app in <dir>` |
| ADVISOR wired in | `Wire ADVISOR into the app` |
| `--sail` | `Use Sail for the local runtime (compose.yaml, laravel/sail in require-dev)` |
| `--docker` | `Use Docker for the local runtime (Dockerfile, compose.yaml, MySQL 8.4)` |

`--sail` and `--docker` are for the Laravel paths: the raw paths run on plain PHP, and combining either flag with a raw permutation is refused.

### Related[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/plan-format.html#related)

- [Commands](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html)
- [Wiring the stack in](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/wiring-the-stack.html)

Source: https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/templates.html

## Templates[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/templates.html#templates)

Reference for the template directories under `templates/`: which directory bakes which shape, what each one carries, the Squire-owned deploy copy, and the rules the generator applies before it writes anything. Pick a shape first in [Pick a shape](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/shapes.html), then come back here for the exact values.

Five jars on the shelf, all five full in 0.1.

![The proof: dough rises past its gold band as WayneUI, SESAME, HELMET, PROCTOR and Preflight go in one by one, over the feeding schedule](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/readme/proof.svg)

### The template directories[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/templates.html#the-template-directories)

| Directory | Shape | Status in 0.1 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `raw/` | Raw PHP with WayneUI's standalone path | generates |
| `raw-vue/` | Raw PHP + Vue SPA over JSON, layered over `raw/` | generates |
| `laravel-blade/` | Laravel + Blade | generates |
| `laravel-blade-vue/` | Laravel + Blade + Vue islands | generates |
| `laravel-inertia/` | Laravel + Inertia/Vue | generates |
| `squire/` | Squire's exported deploy files, not a shape | installed as-is into every app |

The flags that select a shape:

| Flags | Permutation |
| --- | --- |
| (none) or `--raw` | Raw PHP with WayneUI's standalone path |
| `--raw --vue` | Raw PHP + Vue SPA over JSON |
| `--laravel` | Laravel + Blade |
| `--laravel --vue` | Laravel + Blade + Vue islands |
| `--laravel --inertia` (or `--inertia`) | Laravel + Inertia/Vue |

All five permutations generate in 0.1. `--raw --vue` is the raw PHP bake with a Vue 3 front end over it: PHP answers JSON under `/api/`, Vite builds the Vue app, and `src/Vite.php` loads it from the build or the dev server.

Bake commands for the five shapes:

raw

```bash
sourdough new my-app --raw
```

raw + vue

```bash
sourdough new my-app --raw --vue
```

laravel

```bash
sourdough new my-app --laravel
```

laravel + vue

```bash
sourdough new my-app --laravel --vue
```

inertia

```bash
sourdough new my-app --inertia
```

### What each template carries[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/templates.html#what-each-template-carries)

#### raw/[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/templates.html#raw)

- Pins WayneUI 2.0.8 (`https://wayneui.apps.wayne.edu/v2/releases/2.0.8/wayne-ui.php`) instead of fetching the floating `main` branch copy.
- Ships Pinstripe's coding standard: `pint.json` (the per preset, with the fetched `public/wayne-ui.php` kept out and `vendor` excluded) and `phpstan.neon` (Pinstripe's raw preset, level 8 over `src/` and `public/`), with `waynestate/pinstripe` in require-dev and the extension-installer plugin allowed.
- Ships `scripts` (`test`, `lint`, `fix`, `analyse`, `proctor`, `ci`) and `scripts-descriptions`, so a generated raw app can run its own gate locally with `composer ci`, which runs test, lint, analyse, proctor and audit in that order.
- Its `.gitlab-ci.yml` runs an explicit `composer-ci` job (`composer install`, then `composer ci`), mirroring the Laravel overlay, so PROCTOR sees a `composer ci` in the pipeline instead of warning that no job runs it.
- Ships `stubs/wayne-ui.php`, a static-analysis stub for the run-time WayneUI functions (`wsu_shell_start`, `wsu_shell_end`) that `phpstan.neon` scans through `scanFiles`, so `composer ci` in a freshly baked raw app no longer fails with function-not-found errors for functions that arrive only with the fetched `public/wayne-ui.php`.
- The front controller answers `404` for any path but `/` (a short not-found page that keeps WayneUI's layout and links home) instead of rendering the home page for every URL; `/up` stays HELMET's and answers first.
- Installs Squire's deploy files from `templates/squire/`: `build.sh`, `deployments/001-first-release.sh`, `scripts/release.sh`, `scripts/parity.sh`, `scripts/parity.ps1`, `health.php`, `public/up.php`, `docker-compose.squire.yml`, `.env.squire.example`, and the `.squire/` build context.
- Oracle: raw PHP apps run queries through the `App\Oracle` helper, which takes values only as binds and answers mistakes with plain sentences.

#### raw-vue/[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/templates.html#raw-vue)

`sourdough new --raw --vue` copies `raw/` first, then `raw-vue/` over it, so the two raw shapes share the same Squire files, Pinstripe checks, Oracle helper, Playbook and ADVISOR wiring. The manifest records the template as `raw-vue`.

- `public/index.php` boots HELMET, the session and SESAME exactly as `raw/` does. Paths under `/api/` answer JSON: `/api/me` returns the signed-in user (`username` and `name`), an unknown endpoint is a JSON `404`, and a request without a session is a JSON `401` instead of a redirect to CAS. `/` sends the page that loads the Vue app; any other path sends the same page with a `404`, and Vue says the page does not exist.
- `src/Vite.php` prints the stylesheet, `modulepreload` and script tags for `resources/js/app.js` from `public/build/manifest.json` (imported chunks and their CSS included), each with HELMET's CSP nonce. While `npm run dev` runs, `public/hot` holds the dev server's origin and the helper points at it instead, and adds it to the CSP; with `APP_ENV=production` the hot file is ignored. `tests/ViteTest.php` covers both paths.
- `package.json` pins `@waynestate/wayne-ui-css` and `@waynestate/wayne-ui-vue` 2.0.8 exactly, as the Inertia shape does, with Vue 3 and Vite 6. `resources/css/app.css` imports WayneUI's layered `dist/wayne-ui.css`, and `resources/js/App.vue` draws the page with WayneUI's app bar, environment ribbon, cards and footer, served from the app's own origin (no CDN).
- `vite.config.js` builds into `public/build` with the manifest at its top, keeps `public/` (PHP's document root) out of the copy, and writes and removes `public/hot` around the dev server. `.gitignore` adds `/node_modules/`, `/public/build/` and `/public/hot`: Squire's release script runs `npm ci` and `npm run build` once `package-lock.json` is committed.
- Drops `stubs/wayne-ui.php` and `phpstan.neon`'s `scanFiles`: Vue draws the chrome, so there is no fetched `public/wayne-ui.php`.
- Its `.gitlab-ci.yml` adds a `frontend` job (`npm install`, `npm run build`) to the raw pipeline.

#### laravel-blade/[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/templates.html#laravel-blade)

- A fresh Laravel skeleton from Composer, the laravel-blade overlay, the stack packages, Squire's laravel deploy files and the manifest.
- Ships `app/Providers/AppServiceProvider.php` with `Schema::defaultStringLength(191)`, so string columns stay inside Citadel's MySQL 5.6 index limit (PROCTOR `mysql56-string-default`).
- The views read the signed-in user as an array (`$user['name']`), because SESAME's `Sesame::user()` returns an array, not an object.
- Next steps: `composer install`, `cp .env.example .env`, `php artisan key:generate`, `php artisan migrate`, `php artisan serve`.

#### laravel-blade-vue/[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/templates.html#laravel-blade-vue)

- The Laravel + Blade bake under a front-end layer: Vite with the Vue plugin, a `resources/js/app.js` registry that mounts a Vue 3 app on every `[data-vue-island]` element, and a Counter island live on the dashboard view.
- Ships `tests/Feature/ExampleTest.php` with `$this->withoutVite()`, so `composer ci` in a freshly baked islands app does not fail on the missing Vite manifest before `npm run build` has run.
- Next steps: the Laravel + Blade steps plus `npm install` and `npm run build`.

#### laravel-inertia/[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/templates.html#laravel-inertia)

- The same Laravel skeleton, the laravel-inertia overlay (Inertia pages rendered by Vue, Ziggy routes, the stack packages), Squire's laravel deploy files and the manifest.
- Ships `AppServiceProvider` (string length 191 for Citadel's MySQL 5.6) and a `tests/TestCase.php` that writes a stub Vite manifest, so view tests boot without a build.
- The `.gitlab-ci.yml` carries the `ziggy` job: it regenerates `resources/js/ziggy.*` and fails on any diff, so the route list that ships inside the Vite bundle always matches the routes.
- The overlay allows `phpstan/extension-installer`; the appended SESAME and HELMET env keys ship commented out (except `SESAME_DRIVER=fake`) so package defaults hold instead of being overridden by empty values. `config/sesame.php` defaults `SESAME_FAKE_USERNAME` to `jane.doe`, so the fake driver has a non-empty username.
- Next steps: the Laravel + Blade steps plus `npm install` and `npm run build`.

### Shared wiring in every app[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/templates.html#shared-wiring-in-every-app)

| Part | What lands in the app |
| --- | --- |
| Stack packages | HELMET `^0.3`, SESAME `^0.4`, PROCTOR `^0.4` |
| Playbook | `waynestate/playbook` in `require`, the VCS repository, `config.gitlab-domains` so Composer sends your token to git.wayne.edu, the seven setting names in `.env.example`, a `composer playbook` script that shows whether Playbook is installed, and a "WSU values (PLAYBOOK)" README section that explains how to get read access |
| ADVISOR | `waynestate/advisor` in `require-dev`, `.mcp.json` git-ignored (a client config starts a program for whoever opens the project), a README "ADVISOR" section; install with `php vendor/bin/advisor install --client=claude --write` |
| Preflight | `.gitlab-ci.yml` pins the Preflight CI components to the 0.1.4 release SHA (`79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8`, with the tag in a trailing comment), because PROCTOR 0.4's `preflight-pinned` check wants a 40-hex SHA |
| Oracle | wired but dormant: `ORACLE_USERNAME`, `ORACLE_PASSWORD`, and either `ORACLE_TNS` or `ORACLE_HOST`, `ORACLE_PORT`, `ORACLE_SERVICE_NAME` ship commented out in `.env.example`; while they are empty, nothing connects and nothing errors. Laravel apps check the wiring with `php artisan oracle:check` |
| Manifest | `.sourdough/manifest.json`: the Sourdough version, the template, the answers you chose, and a sha256 hash of every file, each marked `managed` or `seeded` |

Seeded files are `.env.example` and `README.md`: Sourdough wrote them once and you own them now. Managed files belong to Sourdough; the manifest is the record a later `sourdough feed` refreshes. See [The manifest](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/manifest.html).

Note

`--playbook` is kept for compatibility and changes nothing; `--no-playbook` skips the Playbook wiring and is for CI and automated tests only. WSU apps need Playbook. `--no-advisor` skips the ADVISOR wiring.

### The Squire-owned copy (`templates/squire/`)[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/templates.html#the-squire-owned-copy-templates-squire)

The deploy files in your app come from Squire's exported copy, checked into this repository at `templates/squire/`: `raw/`, `laravel/`, `static/`, `vue/`, `catalog.json`, `manifest.json`. Squire owns those files; Sourdough never hand-edits them, installs them as-is and records them in the manifest, so you never edit them by hand.

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `composer squire-copy:sync` | rewrites the copy from the installed `waynestate/squire` package (dev dependency `^0.4`) |
| `composer squire-copy:check` | exits 1 when the committed copy has drifted; part of `composer ci` |

When Squire's templates change, regenerate the copy from a Squire checkout, then verify it:

```
php ../squire/bin/export-templates.php --to=../sourdough/templates/squire
php ../squire/bin/export-templates.php --to=../sourdough/templates/squire --check
```

Commit the refreshed copy with the Squire commit in the message, and add a CHANGELOG line.

### Rules the generator applies[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/templates.html#rules-the-generator-applies)

From the best-practices notes, section 1 (Generating a project):

| Rule | What it requires | Stack today |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Make the permutation an explicit, validated input | take the permutation from flags (`--raw`, `--vue`, `--laravel`, `--inertia`) and refuse combinations that make no sense, such as `--inertia` without `--laravel` | Documented; step 1 plans tests for every row and for the invalid combinations |
| Offer `--dry-run`, and make it write nothing | print the plan (files, packages, commands) and change nothing on disk | Documented; step 1 plans a test that `--dry-run` writes nothing |
| Refuse a non-empty target | refuse to generate into a directory that already has files; if overwriting is ever allowed, require a `--force` flag and prompt only when the session is interactive | Documented; there is no `--force` design yet |
| Use exit codes that scripts can rely on | 0 on success and distinct non-zero codes for the main failure modes, documented; PROCTOR uses 0 pass, 1 fail, 2 tool error | Not yet; pick one meaning for 2 across the stack before Sourdough ships |
| Keep output friendly to people and to machines | results to stdout and logs, warnings and errors to stderr, `--json` for the plan, color off when output is not a terminal, when `NO_COLOR` is set, or with `--no-color`, prompt only when stdin is a terminal, and `--no-input` so CI and agents never hang | Not yet |
| Test the generator on every permutation, in temp directories | generate each permutation into a temp directory and compare the result with a stored snapshot; test commands through a tester class rather than a real terminal | Documented; Laravel paths need the network, so their tests run in a pipeline job instead of the unit suite |
| Treat names, paths and templates as untrusted input | check `<dir>` and any app or vendor name against an allow-list before the value reaches a file name, a `composer.json` or a command line; refuse any write whose resolved path falls outside the target directory; keep templates as data: placeholder substitution only, with no code in a template running during generation | Enforced for names: `RawGenerator::assertValidName()` checks every name (letter or number first; then letters, numbers, spaces, dots, dashes and underscores; at most 63 characters) before generation touches the disk, and the test suite generates with hostile names (quotes, backslash, newline, NUL byte, `{{app_slug}}`, path traversal, 64 characters, empty, dashes only, leading dash or dot, a Unicode look-alike), asserting the exception and an absent or empty target dir. Paths stay inside the target by construction: the slug is `[a-z0-9-]` only and every write path is built under the target dir |
| Make the "new app" page and the CLI one engine | the page calls the same plan code as `sourdough new --dry-run --json`, shows the equivalent command, validates on the server with the rules above, and returns the same archive the CLI would write; a snapshot test compares the two | Documented for the page itself; Not yet for the shared-engine rule |

Note

The untrusted-input rule exists because scaffolders have turned template content into code execution before: Backstage's scaffolder let anyone who could edit a registered template run code on the host (CVE-2023-35926, fixed in 1.15.0), and Copier refuses templates that use tasks, migrations or Jinja extensions unless the caller passes `--trust`.
